text: On March 5, 2012 and December 30, 2016, the City received a Zoning By-law Amendment application for the north block and south block respectively of the lands then known as 309 Cherry Street, now known as 65 Ookwemin Street (the "Site"). The Site is centrally located within Ookwemin Minising in the Port Lands. The applications collectively proposed mixed use development, with a 26- storey residential tower atop an 8-storey podium and the partial retention of existing heritage buildings on the north block, and an 11-storey building and 52-storey building atop a 4-12 storey 'u-shaped' podium. The applicant appealed City Council's neglect or failure to make a decision on its applications for the Zoning By-law Amendment to the predecessor Ontario Land Tribunal (the "Tribunal") on October 31, 2014 for the north block and June 1, 2017 for the south block (the "Appeals").
